chapter: Southwestern bands and New Orleans youth
title: Troy Floyd's theme and showmanship
summary: Floyd's theme was sung and spoken like Ted Lewis; he was more of a gimmick man but could get jobs.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Possibly so, more than likely in Texas if you could ever find someone that knew Eddie Perry. Did Troy Floyd have a theme? Yes, Troy's theme was, oh, let's go a little further. You have to come in. I'm afraid. I'm afraid someday you'll leave. I'm afraid someday I'll breathe. I'm afraid. It was a beautiful song. And Troy would do a spiel on it. He would talk it. Like what's this guy does is talking on his numbers. He'd sing and then he'd talk it a lot. One of the old, old timers. One of the white... I don't know.
There'd been several. Ted Lewis. There you go. You hit it right on the head. He was like, do that kind of thing?
So he was a showman and a salesman type of guy? He tried to be. Yeah.
But he was more of a gaminer, I'll put it that way.
Well, he must have known the right people if he found jobs by him.
Oh, yes. He could get the jobs.
